Devon R: Quick RFC follow-up: proposing an 'adapter sunset' playbook — safely retire thin adapter layer after extraction instead of long-term maintenance. want short checklist + rollback notes.

Helena M: Sounds good. Why sunset instead of keep-as-fallback? adapters rot and add latency.

Ravi S: Agreed. We need an explicit verification window and a fast rehydrate path in case we need to re-enable adapter quickly.

Devon R: Proposed flow: extract service -> adapter shim in front -> canary -> full cut -> 2w monitoring -> adapter toggle off (soft-sunset) -> 30d wait -> adapter image removed (hard-sunset).

Helena M: Add a pre-sunset freeze: keep adapter code read-only for 14d, run smoke prompts, and keep quick-redeploy manifest.

Ravi S: DB nuance: keep read-shim for 7d after soft-sunset, so we can re-point reads in rollback. also keep incremental backfill checkpoints.

ops-bot: created ticket ARCH-6110: "adapter-sunset-playbook" https://tracker/ARCH-6110

Devon R: Minimal policy for toggle (pseudo):
route: /enrich/v2/score
adapter_enabled: true  # feature-flag:value
canary: 10% -> 100%
monitoring: [latency_p95, error_rate, quality_delta]
rollback_action: flip adapter_enabled -> true

Helena M: telemetry owner? I can own the smoke prompt set and run daily diffs for first 14d.

Ravi S: I'll own the rollback runbook and DB checkpoints. plan: 6d spike for infra + 1d warmup before canary.

Devon R: Meeting Thurs 11 to lock timings. If no blockers we start Monday. thumbs up?

Helena M: +1

Ravi S: +1

Devon R: Closing. I'll post RFC addendum with explicit thresholds and the deploy manifest by EOD Wed.
